questions.question: Define management and explain the difference between being effective and being efficient, using the supermarket as an example.
questions.expected_answer: Management is planning, organising, leading and controlling a business's resources (people, money, equipment, materials, information) to reach its goals, getting work done through other people. Effective: achieving the goal (shelves full, customers satisfied). Efficient: achieving it without wasting resources (no food spoiling from overstocking, no idle paid staff).

questions.question: Compare top, middle and lower management under: who they are, time horizon, kind of decision, and one example of a decision for the supermarket.
questions.expected_answer: Top: owner/MD, general manager, board; long-term (3-5+ years); strategic, whole business, high risk; e.g. open a second branch or start home delivery. Middle: department heads (fresh produce, finance, HR); medium-term (about a year); tactical, one department; e.g. how orders are taken and packed, departmental budget. Lower: supervisors, head baker, shift supervisors; short-term (day/week); operational, routine; e.g. shift roster, which shelves to restock, handling a complaint.

questions.question: Explain the chain of command, how authority, responsibility and information flow, and the meaning of span of control.
questions.expected_answer: Chain of command: line of authority from top to bottom shown on the organisational chart, so each person knows their manager. Authority flows down; responsibility (accountability) flows up; information flows both ways (goals down, reports and problems up). Span of control: the number of people reporting directly to one manager (e.g. a supervisor with six cashiers); too wide weakens supervision, too narrow wastes managers.
